name: Operating Systems
description: The systems that run our computers and phones, from Unix and MS-DOS to Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS.

checkpoints.name: Mainframes and Unix
checkpoints.note: Multics shows what a time-sharing system can do, and Unix, written at Bell Labs, becomes the model for most systems that follow.

checkpoints.name: Systems for the first PCs
checkpoints.note: CP/M runs the first small business computers, MS-DOS ships with the IBM PC in 1981, and the Macintosh brings windows and a mouse in 1984.

checkpoints.name: Windows takes the desktop
checkpoints.note: Windows 3 and then Windows 95 put a graphical desktop on most of the world's PCs. Linux, started by a student in 1991, grows into the system that runs much of the internet.

checkpoints.name: XP and Mac OS X
checkpoints.note: Windows XP and Mac OS X, both released in 2001, set the pattern for the desktop for more than a decade.

checkpoints.name: Phones change everything
checkpoints.note: The iPhone arrives in 2007 and Android a year later. Within a few years they push aside Symbian, webOS and Windows Phone, and most computing moves to the phone.

checkpoints.name: Today
checkpoints.note: Windows 10 and 11 on the desktop, and Android and iOS in the pocket, with Linux underneath much of the rest.
